summary: The Pentagon made two significant moves this week on the whistleblower front: it issued new legal waivers on September 14th aimed at encouraging personnel to disclose UAP information, and followed up with a sixth batch of declassified files on September 18th that included audio from a 1952 Project Blue Book briefing. The waiver announcement drew mixed reactions, with journalist Ross Coulthart questioning whether the new protections truly constitute transparency or merely repackage existing safeguards. Meanwhile, Harvard physicist Avi Loeb flagged an intriguing detail from the released files: multiple sightings involved objects that made no sound, a characteristic that complicates conventional explanations. The releases come as Congress continues pressing for answers about potential recovered craft and non-human technology, with lawmakers noting that public stigma around UAP sightings has shifted even if the fundamental questions remain unchanged after 75 years.
